events.title: CDC Cyclospora Season Surveillance Begins Amid Early Case Surge
events.detail: CDC's routine May 1 start of annual domestic Cyclospora surveillance shows an unusually fast early case pace. By comparison, the CDC received just 1,180 domestically acquired cyclosporiasis case reports between May 1 and August 31, 2025 — a fraction of what would accumulate by mid-summer 2026, an early signal of an outsized season.

events.title: New Cyclospora Cluster Added to FDA's CORE Outbreak Table
events.detail: FDA's Coordinated Outbreak Response and Evaluation (CORE) Network opens a formal outbreak table entry for a growing multistate Cyclospora cluster, the first sign of what would become the largest domestic cyclosporiasis outbreak on record.

events.title: CDC Flags Separate 145-Case Cluster Across 17 States
events.detail: CDC's national surveillance identifies 145 domestically acquired cyclosporiasis cases across 17 states with 20 hospitalizations, tracked separately from the emerging Taylor Farms/Taco Bell investigation. CDC notes it is running several concurrent, unrelated Cyclospora investigations this season.

events.title: Michigan Cyclosporiasis Cases Climb to 572
events.detail: Michigan, which would become the epicenter of the outbreak, reports 572 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases and rising, prompting the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services to intensify its epidemiological investigation into a common food source.

events.title: Taco Bell Pulls Fresh Produce From Stores in Affected States
events.detail: Taco Bell voluntarily removes fresh produce items, including shredded lettuce, from restaurant locations in states with rising cyclosporiasis case counts as a precaution while health officials work to identify the source, ahead of any formal recall.

events.title: CDC Issues Health Alert Network Advisory: 1,645 Confirmed, 5,100+ Probable Cases
events.detail: CDC issues a Health Alert Network (HAN) advisory to clinicians nationwide describing domestically acquired cyclosporiasis cases in multiple U.S. states, reporting 1,645 laboratory-confirmed cases and more than 5,100 probable cases, and urging providers to consider Cyclospora testing for patients with prolonged watery diarrhea.

events.title: CDC and FDA Link Shredded Iceberg Lettuce at Taco Bell to Outbreak
events.detail: Epidemiologic patient-interview data and FDA traceback converge on shredded iceberg lettuce served at Taco Bell locations as the likely common vehicle. Illnesses are ultimately tied to Taco Bell stores in nine states: Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, West Virginia, Kansas, Oklahoma, Illinois, and Pennsylvania. FDA traces the lettuce to a single central-Mexico supplier.

events.title: Taylor Farms de México Recalls All Central-Mexico Iceberg Lettuce
events.detail: Taylor Farms de México voluntarily recalls all iceberg lettuce sourced from its central-Mexico growing region after FDA traceback points to the company as the likely source of contamination. The recalled product, including Walmart's Marketside-brand bagged lettuce in 8-, 12-, 16-, and 24-oz sizes with best-if-used-by dates of July 18–August 3, 2026, was distributed to at least 31 states.

events.title: FDA Retracts Positive Cyclospora Border Sample as False Positive
events.detail: FDA withdraws a Cyclospora-positive test result from a lettuce sample detained at the Laredo, Texas border crossing, stating the result 'does not represent true amplification.' The recall remains in effect despite the retraction, as the traceback and epidemiological case-control evidence still point to the same supplier; no product sample would go on to test positive for Cyclospora over the course of the investigation.

events.title: Multistate Outbreak Expands From 5 to 9 States: 1,947 Illnesses
events.detail: The Taco Bell/Taylor Farms multistate outbreak grows from five to nine states as case counts reach 1,947 illnesses and 98 hospitalizations, with Kansas, Oklahoma, Illinois, and Pennsylvania newly added to the affected-state list.

events.title: House Oversight Democrat Demands Answers From Taylor Farms Over White House Ties
events.detail: Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA), ranking member of the House Oversight Committee, sends a letter to Taylor Farms CEO Bruce Taylor alleging the company may have attempted to influence FDA's outbreak investigation and misled consumers about the recall's scope. Garcia's letter notes Taylor's donation to Trump came less than a week after the administration agreed to delay implementation of FSMA Rule 204, a food-traceability rule, and demands disclosure of all communications with federal agencies and the White House since January 21, 2026.

events.title: North Carolina Reports Separate Cluster Linked to Parsley and Cilantro
events.detail: North Carolina health officials report 718 cyclosporiasis cases and 24 hospitalizations since May 1, tied to a cluster where parsley, cilantro, and lettuce are all under investigation as possible vehicles. State officials say the North Carolina cases do not appear linked to the Taco Bell/Taylor Farms multistate outbreak in other states. NCDHHS launches a public case dashboard the same week.

events.title: Congressional Questioning of Taylor Farms Intensifies
events.detail: House Oversight Committee scrutiny of Taylor Farms broadens into questions about the company's food-safety practices and its influence campaign, as lawmakers press for documentation of communications with FDA and the White House during the outbreak response.

events.title: Combined Nationwide Count Tops 18,000 Cases Across Six Investigations
events.detail: CDC's combined tally across all active Cyclospora investigations — the Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak, the North Carolina cilantro/parsley cluster, and several smaller regional clusters — surpasses 18,000 total reported cases, including 6,707 laboratory-confirmed. Six separate Cyclospora investigations are underway simultaneously, an unprecedented number for a single season.

events.title: Mexican Regulators Inspect Taylor Farms Guanajuato Facility, Find No Contamination
events.detail: Mexico's food-safety regulator COFEPRIS and agri-food agency SENASICA conduct a sanitary inspection of the Taylor Farms de México processing facility in Guanajuato between July 18–20, with laboratory analyses of lettuce and water samples showing no presence of Cyclospora cayetanensis or fecal coliforms. Mexican officials say the inspection found the company maintains a functioning traceability system, and note that the border shipment that produced FDA's since-retracted positive sample never entered the United States.

events.title: First Two Deaths Reported in Michigan Outbreak
events.detail: Michigan health officials report the first two deaths associated with the cyclosporiasis outbreak, both among individuals with underlying health conditions. State officials decline to elaborate further on the specific conditions, drawing some criticism over transparency. These are believed to be among the first cyclosporiasis-associated deaths recorded in the U.S.

events.title: CDC Broadens Outbreak Definition to Include Retail Consumers: 6,358 Cases, 15 States
events.detail: CDC broadens its outbreak case definition beyond Taco Bell patrons to include people who bought the recalled lettuce at retail, pushing the multistate outbreak total to 6,358 domestically acquired cases across 15 states — six newly added — with 278 hospitalizations.

events.title: Michigan Woman Files First Major Lawsuit Against Taco Bell, Taylor Farms
events.detail: A Michigan woman sickened in the outbreak files a lawsuit against Taco Bell and Taylor Farms, alleging negligence in sourcing and serving contaminated lettuce. It is among the earliest of what would become a wave of federal lawsuits tied to the outbreak.

events.title: Michigan Lifts Bagged-Salad Advisory as State Total Reaches 12,485
events.detail: Michigan health officials lift their bagged-salad consumption advisory as the recalled product ages out of shelf life, even as the state's cumulative cyclosporiasis case count climbs to 12,485 — by far the largest state total in the outbreak.

events.title: FDA Begins On-Site Inspection at Taylor Farms Mexico as Case Count Nears 10,000
events.detail: FDA investigators begin an on-site inspection at the Taylor Farms de México facility as the official outbreak case count approaches 10,000. Reporting reveals the FDA had not inspected the facility in seven years — its last visit was in 2019, and before that in 2013 in response to a prior cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to the same company.

events.title: Fourteen Federal Lawsuits Filed Against Taco Bell and Taylor Farms
events.detail: Legal filings continue to mount, with fourteen people having filed federal lawsuits against Taco Bell and Taylor Farms over illnesses tied to the outbreak. Food-safety attorneys, including Marler Clark and Pritzker Hageman, say more suits are likely as the six-week diagnostic lag continues to surface new cases.

events.title: Combined Cases Top 24,000 as CDC Says New-Case Pace Is Slowing
events.detail: CDC reports the combined nationwide tally — 13,895 laboratory-confirmed plus 10,455 additional cases under investigation — has surpassed 24,000, with total hospitalizations across all clusters reaching roughly 1,018 and two deaths. CDC notes the week-over-week growth rate is slowing, with only about 2,000 new cases recorded in the prior week versus a jump of more than 10,000 the week before, though officials caution the six-week reporting lag means the true trend is still uncertain.

events.title: National Multistate Count Reaches 9,481 Across 17 States; Maine, Massachusetts Added
events.detail: CDC's official multistate outbreak count linked to Taylor Farms de México lettuce reaches 9,481 illnesses across 17 states, with Maine and Massachusetts newly added, 398 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths. Michigan's own state dashboard separately shows 13,909 cumulative cases and 314 hospitalizations — a discrepancy CDC attributes to differing counting criteria between the federal multistate case definition and state-level surveillance totals.

events.title: Washington State Reports 67 Cases, Mostly Travel-Linked
events.detail: Washington State Department of Health reports 67 total cyclosporiasis cases since May 1 with 2 hospitalizations and no deaths. Of 65 interviewed cases, 42 had traveled to endemic countries (38 to Mexico); among 22 non-travelers, most had visited states with known outbreak activity, including two residents who contracted the illness after eating at a Taco Bell while visiting Michigan. Washington notes the recalled Taylor Farms lettuce was not distributed to the state.

events.title: Food-Safety Advocates Press FDA Over Lack of Import Alert on Taylor Farms
events.detail: Food-safety watchdogs, including attorney Bill Marler and eFoodAlert, publicly question why FDA has not placed Taylor Farms de México or iceberg lettuce on an import alert requiring detention without physical examination at the border, despite the scale of the outbreak. FDA says its investigation, including the on-site Mexico inspection, remains open and has not resulted in an import alert as of mid-August.

events.title: Season-Wide Surveillance Tops 15,700 Confirmed Cases in 47 States
events.detail: CDC's broadest surveillance figure, which includes travel-associated and unrelated domestic clusters alongside the multistate outbreak, shows more than 15,700 laboratory-confirmed cyclosporiasis cases reported since May 1 across 47 states, with roughly 11,000 additional probable cases still under investigation. This is more than 13 times the 1,180 cases the CDC recorded over the same period in 2025.

events.title: Sen. Warren Demands Answers From RFK Jr. Over 'Calamitous' Outbreak Response
events.detail: Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) sends a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. demanding answers over what she calls the administration's 'calamitous' response to 'the biggest outbreak of cyclosporiasis in U.S. history,' writing that the response 'may be the result of incompetence and corruption.' Warren cites FEC records showing Taylor Fresh Foods made a $1 million donation to MAGA Inc., a pro-Trump PAC, in March 2025, and raises concerns — building on an earlier Wall Street Journal report — that the White House may have worked with Taylor Farms to delay public warnings about the tainted lettuce. She also notes Taco Bell gave consumers earlier, clearer guidance than FDA or CDC did.

media.caption: Sen. Elizabeth Warren questions the administration's handling of the outbreak in a letter to HHS Secretary RFK Jr.

events.title: Combined Season-Wide Count Rises to 27,557 as CDC Confirms 828 Hospitalizations
events.detail: CDC's Aug. 18 weekly surveillance update raises the combined nationwide tally to 27,557 (15,716 laboratory-confirmed plus 11,841 additional cases awaiting lab confirmation or under investigation), an increase of roughly 1,821 confirmed cases from the prior week. CDC now specifies 828 total hospitalizations season-wide, alongside the two Michigan deaths, with cases reported in 47 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. CDC and FDA continue investigating at least six other Cyclospora clusters beyond the Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak with no confirmed source.

media.caption: CDC's Aug. 18 weekly update raises the combined national Cyclospora tally to 27,557 cases.

events.title: Multistate Outbreak Grows to 10,930 Cases; FDA Begins Onsite Sampling at Mexican Lettuce Growers
events.detail: CDC's Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak count climbs to 10,930 illnesses across the same 17 states, with 454 hospitalizations and the two Michigan deaths unchanged. FDA says it has begun onsite inspections and sampling at iceberg lettuce growers in Mexico, working in coordination with Mexican officials, expanding beyond the earlier single-facility inspection at Taylor Farms de México's Guanajuato plant. FDA and CDC state they remain confident all iceberg lettuce tied to this specific outbreak is off the market.

media.caption: The multistate Cyclospora outbreak linked to Taylor Farms lettuce grows to 10,930 illnesses across 17 states.

events.title: Michigan Cases Reach 14,277 as Weekly Growth Drops Sharply; Official Says 'Worst Is Behind Us'
events.detail: Michigan's cumulative cyclosporiasis total reaches 14,277 cases and 335 hospitalizations, up 368 cases and 21 hospitalizations from the prior week — but that weekly increase is down sharply from roughly 1,400 new cases the week before, the smallest weekly gain since late June. Dr. Natasha Bagdasarian, Michigan's chief medical executive, says 'the worst is behind us, at least based on the data we have available to us today,' while cautioning the six-week reporting lag means the cumulative total will keep climbing for weeks after the actual risk has passed.

media.caption: Michigan officials say the state's cyclosporiasis outbreak appears to be slowing after weekly case growth dropped sharply.

events.title: First Illinois Lawsuit Filed Against Taylor Farms Over Cyclospora-Tainted Lettuce
events.detail: Alonso Zaragoza and his wife Jadhira Sanchez sue Taylor Fresh Foods, Inc. and Taylor Farms California, Inc. in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois (case 1:26-cv-10148), the first cyclosporiasis lawsuit of the outbreak filed in Illinois. Zaragoza developed bloody diarrhea after eating a Taco Bell chalupa supreme containing fresh shredded iceberg lettuce ordered July 11; it took 23 days and three separate testing attempts before doctors confirmed Cyclospora on August 4. The ten-count complaint — alleging strict product liability, breach of warranty, negligence, and loss of consortium — names only the two Taylor entities, not any Taco Bell franchisee or corporate entity.

media.caption: A Chicago couple's federal lawsuit becomes the first cyclosporiasis case filed in Illinois against Taylor Farms.

events.title: Watchdog Flags Quiet FDA Expansion of Recalled-Lettuce Distribution to 40 Jurisdictions
events.detail: Food-safety attorney Bill Marler highlights that FDA's Taylor Farms recall notice was quietly revised on August 13 to add nine more states and territories — California, Washington, D.C., Delaware, North Dakota, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Vermont, and Washington state — to the previously reported 31-state distribution footprint, bringing the total to 40 jurisdictions that may have received the recalled iceberg lettuce. Marler notes the change went largely unpublicized: as of his August 23 post, none of the nine newly listed jurisdictions had issued their own public notice to residents.

media.caption: FDA's recalled-lettuce distribution list quietly grew to 40 states and territories as of an August 13 revision.

events.title: Season-Wide Combined Count Rises to 29,024 Across 48 States as Hospitalizations Reach 922
events.detail: CDC's Aug 24-25 weekly surveillance update raises the combined nationwide tally across all seven tracked Cyclospora clusters to 29,024 (17,180 laboratory-confirmed plus roughly 11,844 additional cases still under investigation), up from 27,557 a week earlier. Total hospitalizations season-wide reach 922, with the two Michigan deaths unchanged. Cases now span 48 states and the District of Columbia.

media.caption: CDC's Aug. 24-25 update pushes the combined national Cyclospora tally across all tracked clusters to 29,024 cases.

events.title: North Carolina's Separate Cluster Grows to 940 Cases, 32 Hospitalized
events.detail: NCDHHS data shows the state's parsley/cilantro-linked cyclosporiasis cluster, which health officials maintain is distinct from the Taco Bell/Taylor Farms multistate outbreak, has grown to 940 cases statewide (up from 718 in late July) with 32 hospitalizations. The specific food source in North Carolina remains unidentified.

media.caption: North Carolina's separate cyclosporiasis cluster grows to 940 cases statewide.

events.title: CDC: Multistate Outbreak Expands to 20 States as Georgia, Tennessee, Texas Added; 11,458 Illnesses
events.detail: CDC's regular weekly investigation update adds Georgia, Tennessee, and Texas to the Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak, bringing the total to 20 affected states. Confirmed illnesses climb to 11,458 (from 10,930), with hospitalizations up to 495 (from 454) and the two Michigan deaths unchanged. The last reported illness onset date is Aug 15, 2026. FDA reiterates it 'remains confident that all recalled iceberg lettuce related to this specific cyclospora outbreak is off the market.'

media.caption: CDC's Aug. 27 update expands the Taylor Farms-linked multistate outbreak to 20 states after Georgia, Tennessee, and Texas are added.

events.title: FDA Classifies Taylor Farms Lettuce Recall as Class I, Its Most Serious Designation
events.detail: FDA formally classifies its July 17 recall of Taylor Farms de México central-Mexico iceberg lettuce as Class I — the agency's most serious recall category, reserved for situations where there is 'a reasonable probability' that exposure to a product 'will cause serious adverse health consequences or death.' Cyclospora recalls have historically been classified Class II; officials attribute the escalation to the outbreak's unprecedented scale (11,458 confirmed illnesses across 20 states, 495 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths as of Aug 27) rather than any new positive product test. FDA reiterates it remains 'confident that all recalled iceberg lettuce related to this specific Cyclospora outbreak is off the market' given the product's shelf life has long since expired.

media.caption: FDA classifies the Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce recall as Class I, its most serious designation, amid the ongoing Cyclospora outbreak.

events.title: Michigan's Weekly Count Reaches 14,510 as Growth Continues to Slow
events.detail: Michigan's cumulative cyclosporiasis total climbs to 14,510 cases and 356 hospitalizations, up 233 cases and 21 hospitalizations from the prior week's 14,277/335 figures. The 233-case weekly gain is smaller than the previous week's 368-case increase, continuing the deceleration trend state officials flagged on Aug 20. The two Michigan deaths remain unchanged.

media.caption: Michigan's cyclosporiasis case count reaches 14,510 as weekly growth continues to slow.

events.title: CDC's Official 2026 Cyclospora Season Closes at 17,180 Cases as Three States Go Quiet on Public Reporting
events.detail: CDC's May 1-Aug 31 surveillance season for cyclosporiasis officially closes, with food-safety attorney Bill Marler tallying a federal season total of 17,180 laboratory-confirmed domestically acquired cases, 922 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths across 48 states and DC, and a fifty-state combined count (including probable/pending cases) of 32,857. Marler reports that Virginia (last updated Aug 24, 234 cases), New York (last updated Aug 19, 939 cases), and Ohio (silent since Aug 13, at 5,452 cases) have all stopped publishing public case updates now that the official season has ended, even though the roughly six-week reporting lag means true totals will keep climbing for weeks. He notes only about two-thirds of confirmed cases have been linked to Taylor Farms lettuce — some 5,722 confirmed illnesses remain unattributed to any specific source — and that standard underdiagnosis multipliers suggest the true number of infections, most never tested, could run far higher than the confirmed count.

media.caption: Bill Marler tallies a fifty-state combined Cyclospora case count of 32,857 as CDC's official season closes and several states stop publishing updates.

events.title: Michigan's Weekly Count Reaches 14,718 as Case Growth Ticks Back Up
events.detail: Michigan's cumulative cyclosporiasis total climbs to 14,718 cases and 366 hospitalizations, up 208 cases and 10 hospitalizations from the prior week's 14,510/356 figures — a slightly larger weekly gain than the 233-case increase reported Aug 27, interrupting the deceleration trend state officials had flagged since mid-August. The two Michigan deaths remain unchanged. CDC's separate multistate outbreak count tied to Taylor Farms lettuce remains at 11,458 illnesses across 20 states as of Sept 1, unchanged from Aug 27.

media.caption: Michigan's cyclosporiasis case count reaches 14,718 as of Sept 3, 2026.

events.title: CDC Season-Wide Count Jumps to 18,445 Confirmed Cases as Outbreak Reaches 49 States
events.detail: CDC's Sept 1 data refresh (covering the season through Aug 31) lifts the national lab-confirmed cyclosporiasis total to 18,445, up 1,265 from the Aug 25 figure of 17,180, with season-wide hospitalizations rising to 990 (from 922). The outbreak now spans 49 states plus DC, up from 48. CDC still lists 13,505 additional cases as non-lab-confirmed or pending, plus a further 3,491 cases awaiting classification of domestic vs. international acquisition. The two Michigan deaths remain unchanged. This is a season-wide, all-clusters total distinct from the narrower Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak count, which CDC's outbreak-specific page still lists at 11,458 illnesses across 20 states as of Aug 27.

media.caption: CDC's cyclosporiasis case data summary, updated Sept 1, 2026.

events.title: Indiana Closes Its Cyclospora Count at 2,104 as Reporting States Dwindle to 13 of 41
events.detail: Indiana publishes what it describes as its final cyclosporiasis update of the season, closing its cumulative count at 2,104 cases, according to food-safety attorney Bill Marler's tracking. Marler reports that only 13 of the 41 states that at some point published public Cyclospora case numbers this season still maintain an active dashboard, even as his independently compiled fifty-state floor for combined cases climbs to roughly 33,525 — nearly three times the federal multistate outbreak's 11,458-case attribution. Michigan's own weekly count, also released this week, rose to 14,718 cases and 366 hospitalizations.

media.caption: Indiana closes its Cyclospora count at 2,104 as most states that once published case data go quiet.

events.title: CDC Formally Announces End to Weekly Cyclospora Outbreak Updates
events.detail: CDC revises its Taylor Farms/Taco Bell multistate outbreak investigation page to state it is 'reducing the frequency of web updates on this multistate outbreak as the number of new cases reported declines,' and that 'updates will no longer take place on a weekly basis.' The federal outbreak page remains frozen at the Aug 27 figures — 11,458 confirmed illnesses across 20 states, 495 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths — with no new numbers issued this Thursday for the first time since the outbreak was declared in mid-July.

media.caption: CDC's outbreak investigation page announces it is reducing update frequency as new Cyclospora case reports decline.

events.title: Marler: All Thirteen Congressional Letters on Cyclospora Outbreak Went Unanswered, No Hearing Called
events.detail: A Marler Blog accounting finds that thirteen letters sent by House and Senate members to CDC, FDA, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and Taylor Farms CEO Bruce Taylor between July 14 and August 13 — including Rep. Robert Garcia's and Sen. Elizabeth Warren's inquiries already covered by this tracker — went unanswered, with all eight letters that specified a response deadline passing without a published reply. No congressional hearing on the outbreak has been scheduled. The piece notes unused oversight tools, including the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations' subpoena authority and House Oversight document-request powers, remain on the table as the season's confirmed toll stands at 18,445 cases, 990 hospitalizations, and 2 deaths.

media.caption: Bill Marler tallies thirteen unanswered congressional letters and no scheduled hearing on the 2026 Cyclospora outbreak.
